headline: 30 garment factories shut in Ashulia amid protests for Tk 30,000 minimum wage
summary: Workers are demanding higher pay, an end to blacklisting, and a halt to arbitrary dismissals, leading to road blocks in Ashulia and Mirpur.
details: At least 30 garment factories in and around Kathgara in Ashulia have declared a holiday for today following protests by workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.
The unrest began in the morning, with workers from Naim Knitwear initially stopping work before expanding their protests to other factories in the area.
Police reports indicate that some workers allegedly threw bricks and stones, resulting in a police officer being hospitalized after being struck on the head.
Industrial police also recovered three crude-bomb-like objects from the road in front of a Nasa Group factory in the Nishchintapur area of Ashulia.
Beyond Ashulia, RMG workers also blocked several roads in Dhaka’s Mirpur area this morning to demand the same wage increases.
A trade union representative stated that anger has grown because a promised wage board, which the labour minister had said would be formed by October, was not established.
Government officials announced at a meeting last night that the process of forming the minimum wage board would begin by Sunday, but workers claim the message has not reached them.
The Ashulia Industrial Police-1 superintendent confirmed that police are continuing efforts to persuade workers to return to work and maintain order.
caption:

Police reports indicate that some workers allegedly threw bricks and stones, resulting in a police officer being hospitalized after being struck on the head.

Industrial police also recovered three crude-bomb-like objects from the road in front of a Nasa Group factory in the Nishchintapur area of Ashulia.

Beyond Ashulia, RMG workers also blocked several roads in Dhaka’s Mirpur area this morning to demand the same wage increases.

A trade union representative stated that anger has grown because a promised wage board, which the labour minister had said would be formed by October, was not established.

Government officials announced at a meeting last night that the process of forming the minimum wage board would begin by Sunday, but workers claim the message has not reached them.

headline_marked: Over 5 lakh students fail as [[HSC pass rate hits 22-year low]]
headline: Over 5 lakh students fail as HSC pass rate hits 22-year low
summary: The pass rate for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate examinations fell to 51.62%, with more than 5 lakh students failing under the general education boards.
details: The pass rate in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations fell to a 22-year low, with 5,07,281 students failing under the nine general education boards.
The pass rate stood at 51.62 percent, down from 57.12 percent last year. This is the lowest pass rate since 2004, when it stood at 47.73 percent.
Across all 11 education boards, including Madrasa and Technical boards, a total of 5,94,113 students failed, while the combined pass rate was 52.12 percent.
The number of students securing GPA-5, the highest grade, also hit an eight-year low, with only 40,084 students achieving the top grade across all 11 boards.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon acknowledged that the overall results were unsatisfactory and stated that the government will take steps to address learning gaps.
caption:
Over 5 lakh students failed the HSC exams this year—the lowest pass rate in 22 years.

The pass rate in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations fell to a 22-year low, with 5,07,281 students failing under the nine general education boards.

The pass rate stood at 51.62 percent, down from 57.12 percent last year. This is the lowest pass rate since 2004, when it stood at 47.73 percent.

Across all 11 education boards, including Madrasa and Technical boards, a total of 5,94,113 students failed, while the combined pass rate was 52.12 percent.

The number of students securing GPA-5, the highest grade, also hit an eight-year low, with only 40,084 students achieving the top grade across all 11 boards.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon acknowledged that the overall results were unsatisfactory and stated that the government will take steps to address learning gaps.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo
